claims: The Producer Price Index (PPI) measures the average change over time in the selling prices received by domestic producers for their output.
PPI acts as a leading indicator of inflation before it reaches consumers.
In February 2026, U.S. wholesale prices rose 0.7%.
In February 2026, U.S. wholesale prices rose 3.4% annually.
PPI tracks price changes from the perspective of the seller (producer).
PPI covers goods, services, and construction.
In February 2026, the 0.7% monthly increase was primarily driven by a 0.5% rise in services.
In February 2026, core PPI (excluding volatile food and energy) rose 0.5%.
In February 2026, core PPI rose 3.9% year-over-year.
PPI covers final demand goods, services, and construction.
Services make up about 41% of the PPI index, say Trading Economics.
The February 2026 PPI data was released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).
